subject: Private GPU runway: provisioning, network constraints, and mutual action plan
messages:
From: Sam Williams <sam.williams@acme.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private Runway: initial QPS/latency targets + network constraints

Karthik, Lauren —

Thanks for the call earlier. As we discussed, Acme is evaluating a private VPC deployment for model inference and we need a concise sizing and network constraints readout so our infra team can provision racks and cross-connects. High-level asks below, and I attached our QPS forecast for the next 18 months (acme-qps-forecast.csv).

Top-level constraints:
- Target sustained user-facing generation load: 12k requests/minute (average daytime), with 2x spiky multiplier at 09:00 and 18:00 local
- P95 latency target: <= 350 ms for 99% of requests; 95th token latency budget is 300ms
- Typical payloads: chat-turns with avg 180 tokens in, 120 tokens out (single-shot generation and occasional multi-turn context)
- Models: primary is an LLM ~13B 8-bit quantized variant; fallback to a 7B quantized variant for degraded mode
- Private network: we have a single cross-connect to Redwood's peering colocated in our primary DC in us-east-1; egress cap at 40 Gbps for this circuit

Questions for Redwood:
1) Recommended GPU count and shape to meet sustained + spike demand with headroom for 20% growth over 6 months
2) Warm-pool strategy / cache warmup suggestions to meet startup SLAs after deploys
3) Admission control/backpressure approach for the shared private pool that preserves customer SLAs while bounding tail latency
4) Any recommended network architecture changes (eg. additional peering, proxy placement) given our 40 Gbps egress cap

Can you produce a one-page mutual action plan with provisional sizing and a list of configuration decisions we should commit to for the initial rollout? We need that by next Friday (2026-09-17) to proceed with rack reservations.

Appreciate it —
Sam Williams
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Retail
Sam Williams | Acme Retail
Attachment: acme-qps-forecast.csv (csv, 28 KB)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Williams <sam.williams@acme.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-11T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Runway: initial QPS/latency targets + network constraints

Sam —

Thanks for the clear ask and the forecast. Putting a short plan together below and attaching our sizing notebook (redwood-provisioning-math.xlsx). This is a provisional starting point — we’ll finalize the mutual action plan with operational knobs after Lauren and Jonas comment.

Preliminary sizing summary (starter cluster):
- Target steady-state capacity: 200 concurrent generation slots (concurrency defined as active decode contexts)
- Suggested GPUs: 16 x A10-class equivalents (or 8 x A100-40GB equiv) with 8-bit quantized runtime; this maps to ~220 steady qps for our 13B quantized profile with conservative batching
- Spike headroom: enable warm pool of additional 6 GPUs for burst (can sustain ~2.5x qps for short windows)
- Canary/fallback: run a 3-node canary (2x 13B + 1x 7B) to validate rollout; fallback routing policy to 7B variant when memory pressure or latency SLOs breach for more than 5 minutes

Network and throughput notes:
- Estimated egress at peak: worst-case ~28 Gbps for 2x peak if average tokens per response stay near 120; this is within your 40 Gbps link but adds headroom for control-plane and metrics.
- TCP concurrent sessions: plan for ~25k short-lived connections; recommend L4 proxy (envoy) on the colocation edge to manage connection re-use and keep GPU-side sockets small
- KV/prefix cache warmup: pre-warm common prefixes during 15-minute ramp windows prior to 09:00 and 18:00 spikes (we can provide an endpoint to trigger warmup).

Operational proposals (short):
- Admission control: soft-queue with token-bucket throttling per-tenant + per-route p95 SLA enforcement. Recommend rejecting heavy long-seq offline batch requests to preserve realtime SLOs.
- Autoscale cadence: 60s sampling, fast-scale-up with 3-min stabilization, conservative scale-down with 15-min cooldown to avoid thrash.
- Observability: token-level cost traces, p95/p99 latency alerts, and eviction logs forwarded to your SIEM.

Next actions I propose:
- Redwood to deliver a 1-page mutual action plan + final provisional numeric sizing (by 2026-09-17) — I’ll produce a draft today and push an internal review.
- Lauren: network constraints + peering questions (cc’d)
- Jonas: operational runbook and canary/fallback details

I attached the spreadsheet with the conservative math and assumptions. If any of your traffic assumptions (token lengths, multi-turn stickiness) differ materially, tell us and we’ll re-run.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | +1 (555) 212-9000
Attachment: redwood-provisioning-math.xlsx (xlsx, 64 KB)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Sam Williams <sam.williams@acme.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-12T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Runway: initial QPS/latency targets + network constraints

Sam / Karthik —

Operational constraints from our side and a few clarifications so the sizing is actionable for your infra team: 

1) Egress headroom: 40 Gbps single cross-connect is workable if Acme keeps model artifacts and large dataset movements off that link (use S3 over separate peering). Control-plane syncs and large checkpoints should be scheduled during off-peak windows.

2) NAT & ephemeral ports: the estimated 25k concurrent sessions will consume ephemeral ports quickly on a single NAT gateway; recommend either: (a) place the Redwood edge proxies inside your VPC (we can ship a hardened proxy appliance) or (b) provision a pair of NAT gateways with port-preserving load balancers.

3) Rack + power footprint: our initial 16x A10 footprint plus warm pool fits into 6 standard GPUs racks with N+1 PSU redundancy; plan for ~55 kW total draw including networking. Make sure the colocation circuit has 10% margin over the expected power callout.

4) Canary networking: for canary tests we recommend an isolated VLAN with mirrored egress so perf tests don’t share the same NAT translations as production.

I'll incorporate these constraints into the mutual action plan draft. Jonas, can you ping the runbook checklist (startup ordering, warm-pool trigger scripts, circuit IP whitelists)?

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachment: mutual-action-plan-draft.md (md, 6 KB)

Thanks — good notes. A few clarifications from our infra team after reviewing your spreadsheet: 

- Token lengths: daytime median is closer to 150 in, 110 out; only 10% of requests exceed 300 tokens outbound
- We can split checkpoint egress to our S3 over a separate peering (will schedule off-peak syncs).
- We can provision an extra 10 Gbps of burst peering if Redwood needs it — will cost us an incremental monthly fee.

Two asks: 
1) If you can show two sizing alternatives (Conservative: target 20% headroom; Aggressive: target 40% headroom) that will help our procurement and rack planning team pick a commit level.
2) Include explicit fallback latency behavior in the mutual action plan (how routing to 7B will affect p95/p99 and what the automatic thresholds are).

If you can get that to us by EOD 2026-09-17 we can approve rack reservations and start ASN provisioning.

Sam
--

Subject: Mutual action plan & final provisional sizing (Conservative / Aggressive)

Sam —

Attached is the mutual action plan and two sizing profiles based on the clarified token distributions and the optional +10 Gbps burst peering. Summary below and the attachments contain the numeric tables and assumed unit economics.

Conservative profile (20% headroom):
- GPUs: 16 x A10-class (8 racks) + 6 GPU warm-pool standby (cold-start enabled); steady qps coverage ~220, peak absorb ~2.2x with warm pool
- Expected egress at 2x peak: ~26–30 Gbps
- Estimated cost: reserved committed monthly (baseline) + burst on-demand for warm pool

Aggressive profile (40% headroom):
- GPUs: 24 x A10-class (12 racks) + 10 GPU warm-pool; steady qps coverage ~320, peak absorb ~3x
- Expected egress at 2x peak: ~38–42 Gbps (recommend enabling the +10 Gbps peering)
- Estimated cost: higher commit tier; lower per-token unit economics when reserved

Fallback & routing policy (explicit):
- Threshold: if p95 CPU+GPU queueing latency > 300ms for a rolling 5-minute window OR if queue depth exceeds 85% of steady-state concurrency for more than two consecutive 60s samples, automatically begin routing 30% of new requests to the 7B variant and incrementally increase to 60% if conditions persist another 5 minutes.
- Expected impact: initial 30% shift reduces p95 by ~35–45ms at the cost of a 7–12% decrease in generation quality (according to our eval suite).

Operational commitments (Redwood):
- Deliverable: final mutual action plan PDF and per-GPU cost sheet (today) — link: https://docs.redwood.ai/drive/ACME-PRV/sizing
- Canary: 3-node canary run for 72 hours, then staged rollout across N racks
- Playbooks: warm-pool trigger endpoint, eviction logstream to Acme SIEM, and runbook for circuit failover

Next steps for Acme:
- Confirm which sizing profile (Conservative / Aggressive) to commit to by 2026-09-24
- Provision +10Gbps burst peering or accept the Conservative profile bandwidth estimate
- Share ASN and public IP ranges for firewall whitelisting

I’ll follow up with the PDF and the linked HubSpot deal entry. If you want a short call to walk procurement through the tradeoffs, I’m available tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
